newsitem.title: USA: Judge orders Delaware officials to let teens leave.
newsitem.headline: Judge orders Delaware officials to let teens leave.

text.p: A state judge Wednesday gave prison officials until Feb. 4 to allow a teenaged couple accused of killing their newborn son to return to their New Jersey homes to await trial.

Amy Grossberg and Brian Peterson, both 18, were released on $300,000 bail last week pending trial but were required to remain in Delaware until arrangements could be made for out-of-state electronic monitoring. But the arrangements have been delayed by a dispute among state officials over who is responsible for the monitoring.

In a letter to Correction Commissioner Stanley Taylor, Delaware state Judge Henry duPont Ridgely said, "While the defendants have urged an earlier time, I am providing you this time period to resolve the matter of their current placement without the need for further proceedings."
A copy of the the letter was released to Reuters.
Correction Department spokesman Anthony Farina said in a statement the department had not yet received the judge's order and would respond Thursday.
He had said earlier that telephone lines used to monitor prisoners' ankle cuffs work only within Delaware.

"We have some serious concerns about the (department's) authority and ability to effectively implement (last week's) court order ... The defendants will be three hours away. If a situation needs a response, the question is, who will respond?" Farina said.

The bail conditions for Grossberg and Peterson included provisions that they live at home with their families in Wyckoff, New Jersey, be electronically monitored, and observe a curfew of 6 a.m. to 8 p.m., which would allowed them to work and take classes.

Grossberg and Peterson have been staying in separate homes in Delaware and electronically monitored since Ridgely's bail order last week. They face a trial on Sept. 9 on first-degree murder charges in connection with the death of their newborn son, who was found dead in a motel trash bin last November.
